public.S0: On 27 February 2022 the Security Council adopted resolution 2623 (2022) by 11 votes in favour, one against (Russia) and three abstentions (China, India and the United Arab Emirates). Russia's negative vote did not prevent adoption.
public.S1: The Council decided to call an emergency special session of the General Assembly to examine the Ukraine question on the agenda of its 8979th meeting. The resolution recorded that a lack of unanimity among permanent members at that earlier meeting had prevented the Council from exercising its primary responsibility.

S2.speaker: Brazil
S2.passage: Brazil said it voted in favour despite reservations about the timing of the resolution and whether it would contribute to peace. It said urgency warranted adding the General Assembly's voice. Brazil stressed that the Council had yet to exhaust its instruments for supporting a negotiated and diplomatic solution.
fields: supported the resolution despite reservations about timing or contribution to peace

S3.speaker: Russian Federation
S3.passage: After presiding over the vote, Nebenzia explicitly spoke as Russia's representative. Russia explained its negative vote by objecting to the draft recording the Council's inability to uphold its primary responsibility. He distinguished this vote from Russia's veto of draft S/2022/155 at the earlier meeting.
fields: explicitly attributes the post-vote view to Nebenzia's national capacity

S4.speaker: India
S4.passage: India called for an immediate end to violence and advocated diplomacy and dialogue. It welcomed the parties' announcement of talks at the Belarus border. India highlighted stranded Indian nationals and students, disruption to evacuation at border crossings, and the need for uninterrupted, predictable movement.
